Package architecture

Pablo Fuenzalida

2026-05-27

Source: vignettes/architecture-and-functions.Rmd
architecture-and-functions.Rmd

Start here if you are new

Sharkipedia (sharkipedia.org) is a website/database of shark and ray life-history traits and population trends, each tied to a literature reference.

sharkipediaR downloads public species pages, reads the HTML tables, and gives you clean R data frames. You do not need to know how the website is built.

How the package is organised (one sentence)

Each sp_*() function fetches a page → parses tables → cleans names → checks columns → returns a tibble. That split keeps the code maintainable when the website changes.

Function reference (arguments & returns)

Detailed reference for exported sp_*() helpers. For narrative walkthroughs, continue to the sections below.

Discovery

sp_species_urls(all_pages = FALSE, max_pages = NULL, cache = TRUE)

Scrapes the public species index and returns a deduplicated tibble.

Argument Description
all_pages If TRUE, walk all paginated index pages (~65). Default FALSE (first page only, polite).
max_pages Cap pages when all_pages = TRUE (e.g. max_pages = 3 while testing).
cache Use in-session memoised HTTP cache.

Returns: species (scientific name), slug (URL slug), url (full Sharkipedia URL).

sp_search(query, index = NULL, all_pages = FALSE, cache = TRUE)

Case-insensitive substring search on scientific names and slugs.

Argument Description
query Character vector of search terms (e.g. "Carcharhinus").
index Optional tibble from sp_species_urls(). Pass a full index to avoid re-downloading.
all_pages Used only if index is NULL — whether to build a full index first.

Returns: Matching rows from the index (species, slug, url).

Species-level data

sp_species(species, cache = TRUE)

Taxonomy and provenance for one species.

Argument Description
species Scientific name ("Carcharhinus acronotus"), slug, or full species URL.

Returns: One-row tibble: species, superorder, subclass, order, family, source_url, retrieved_at.

sp_traits(species, cache = TRUE)

Life-history trait measurements in long format.

Argument Description
species One name/URL or a character vector for batch download (adds species_input column).

Returns:

Column Description
trait_group Age, Length, Reproduction, Ecological Role, …
trait_name e.g. Amat50, Linf, Lmax-observed
value Reported value (character; use as.numeric() when needed)
standard Units or category (e.g. Year, cm)
value_type Often mean, median, …
sex Male, Female, Pooled, …
location Study or geographic location
reference Sharkipedia reference ID
source_url, retrieved_at Provenance

sp_trends(species, cache = TRUE)

Population abundance trends parsed from embedded chart data on species pages (long format: one row per year).

Argument Description
species One name/URL or character vector (batch).

Returns:

Column Description
location Trend region / stock description
unit e.g. individual, kg
reference Source reference ID
trend_id, trend_url Sharkipedia trend record
year, value Time series observations
species, source_url, retrieved_at Provenance

sp_references(species, cache = TRUE)

Bibliographic reference links cited on the species page (from trait and trend tables).

Returns: reference_id, reference_url, species, source_url, retrieved_at.

Offline helpers

example_carcharhinus(), example_reid2011_trends(), example_white_shark_trends()

Pre-parsed tibbles for examples, tests, and vignettes without HTTP. example_carcharhinus() returns a list (species_meta, traits, trends, references, species_index); the trend helpers return trend tibbles for tutorial species sets.

sp_species_urls() — find species web addresses

What it does: Reads the species index and returns names + URLs.

How to use: Start here when you need a species list. Default = first page only (polite). Use all_pages = TRUE for the full catalogue (slow).

Example:

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))
library(sharkipediaR)

idx <- sp_species_urls()
idx %>% slice_head(n = 5)

sp_search() — search by name

What it does: Filters the index for partial scientific names (e.g. "Carcharh").

How to use: Pass your own index if you already called sp_species_urls(all_pages = TRUE) — avoids re-downloading.

Example:

sp_search("Galeocerdo", index = idx)

sp_species() — taxonomy for one species

What it does: Returns one row: species name, order, family, etc., plus when/where it was downloaded.

Example:

sp_species("Carcharodon carcharias")

sp_traits() — life-history measurements

What it does: All trait rows from a species page (age at maturity, length, reproduction, …) in long format — one row per measurement.

How to use: Pass one name or a vector of names for batch downloads.

Example:

traits <- sp_traits("Carcharodon carcharias")
traits %>%
  filter(trait_name == "Linf") %>%
  mutate(value = as.numeric(value))

sp_trends() — population trends through time

What it does: Extracts year–value series from trend charts on the species page (the same data behind Sharkipedia’s plots).

How to use: Filter by reference to match a paper (see the Ecological workflows tutorial for reid2011).

Example:

trends <- sp_trends("Carcharodon carcharias")
trends %>%
  filter(reference == "reid2011") %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, value)) +
  geom_line()

sp_references() — literature links on a species page

What it does: Lists reference IDs (e.g. reid2011) and URLs cited on that species page.

Example:

sp_references("Carcharodon carcharias")

example_carcharhinus(), example_reid2011_trends(), example_white_shark_trends()

What they do: Frozen Sharkipedia data for tutorials and testing — no internet required.

Example:

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))
library(sharkipediaR)

example_reid2011_trends() %>% count(species)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 2
#>   species                         n
#>   <chr>                       <int>
#> 1 Carcharias taurus              60
#> 2 Carcharodon carcharias         60
#> 3 Galeocerdo cuvier              60
#> 4 Heterodontus portusjacksoni    60
#> 5 Notorynchus cepedianus         60
#> 6 Sphyrna zygaena                60
#> 7 Squatina australis             60

fetch_page() — advanced

What it does: Downloads raw HTML only. Use this if you extend the package; most people should use sp_*() instead.

Example:

# fetch_page("https://www.sharkipedia.org/species/carcharodon-carcharias")

Behind the scenes (optional reading)

Step File Role
Download fetch.R Polite HTTP, rate limit, cache
Read HTML parse.R Find tables and trend JSON
Tidy clean.R snake_case columns, provenance
Check validate.R Required columns present

You never need to call these directly unless you are contributing to sharkipediaR.

Be a good citizen

  • Do not hammer the site with parallel requests.
  • Keep source_url and retrieved_at in your outputs.
  • Cite Sharkipedia and the original papers (e.g. Reid et al. 2011).
